summary: Traffic quarantine activates during canary -> silent model swap observed for pinned tenants
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NimbleDocs) reports that during a gradual canary rollout we triggered a traffic-quarantine path on the edge which resulted in an unexpected model swap for some pinned sessions. The swap was not reflected in logs at the canary-coordinator level and the tenant experienced increased response variance and a brief spike in generation errors (502/504).

Impact:
- ~12% of NimbleDocs traffic in us-east during the window returned responses from a different model variant despite an explicit tenant pin to redwood-open-7b-v1.
- Increased latency and 502/504 observed for affected requests for ~3 minutes.
- Customer-facing incidents (errors and degraded throughput) for mission-critical flow.

Environment:
- prod-us-east, dedicated pool for NimbleDocs (tenant-id: nmbl-1122)
- Active canary rollout: weight shifting 5% -> 25% over 30m
- Traffic quarantine feature enabled for edge to isolate noisy upstreams

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-12 09:03 UTC: Canary weight change initiated via console (canary-coordinator).
- 2026-03-12 09:15 UTC: Edge detected elevated error rate on a small subset and applied traffic-quarantine rules for a group of connections.
- 2026-03-12 09:17 UTC: Customer reports sporadic errors and model mismatch (pin present at request level).
- 2026-03-12 09:20-09:23 UTC: Error spike subsides after quarantine expires but ~3 min window shows mixed-model responses.

Steps to reproduce (attempted):
1) Recreate canary config used by customer (same models and weights) in staging.
2) Simulate elevated error responses from a backend replica to trigger traffic-quarantine behavior at the edge.
3) Send pinned-session requests from a synthetic tenant who has pin metadata set and observe routing headers and final model choice.

Expected behavior:
- Traffic quarantine should isolate problematic upstreams but must preserve explicit tenant model pins and session affinity. A pinned request must not be silently diverted to a different model variant.

Actual behavior:
- Some pinned requests were routed to the quarantine fallback path which allowed fallback to a compatible model variant (quantized variant) and bypassed tenant pin enforcement for the duration of the quarantine.

Logs & Observations:
- Edge logs show quarantine rule id QRTN-1221 applied at 09:15:12 UTC with condition matched: replica-error-rate > 8%.
- Routing audit logs include entries where route resolution returned model redwood-open-7b-v1-quant while request metadata contained tenant_pin=redwood-open-7b-v1.
- Canary-coordinator trace did not show an explicit pin override; it reported requests routed to primary cohort.
- Serving-runtime metrics during the window reported increased KV cache misses for pinned sessions that hit the quantized variant.

Attachments:
- links to sample edge log snippets and routing-audit traces (redwood-logs://nmbl-1122/2026-03-12/09:15-09:25)
comments: 2026-03-12 09:30 - Aisha Kapoor (Support): Initial triage — opened ticket after customer supplied routing logs showing mixed model responses. Escalated to SRE and serving-runtime. Notifying account exec.

2026-03-12 10:05 - Marco Li (SRE): Confirmed quarantine window in edge logs. Correlated routing-audit entries show model selection mismatch for 73 requests. Adding component owners. Marking as Sev1 due to customer impact.

2026-03-12 11:12 - Mei Chen (Serving Runtime): Observed KV cache misses and tokenization-time variance for requests hitting the quantized variant. Hypothesis: quarantine path bypasses pin-enforcement middleware when performing emergency fallback.

2026-03-12 12:00 - Customer (NimbleDocs Support): We saw a spike in failures and inconsistent outputs; temporary mitigation (client-side retry) helped but requests returned different answer styles. Customer requests ETA on fix.

2026-03-13 08:45 - Marco Li (SRE): Reproduced in staging. Traffic-quarantine code path calls routing.resolve_fallback() which does not check tenant_pin header in current implementation (shipped for fast isolation). Preparing patch to add pin preservation check.
investigation_notes: Edge quarantine implementation intentionally relaxed routing constraints to speed isolation; this allowed fallback selection to consider compatible models without verifying tenant_pin.
Routing-audit shows that quarantine introduces short-circuit that skips PinReconciler step under high-error conditions.
Reproduction in staging confirmed the same behavior: enabling quarantine and forcing replica errors causes pinned sessions to be diverted to a fallback model.

Scope: likely affects any tenant using dedicated pools with traffic-quarantine enabled AND active canary rollouts where fallback models exist. We believe this is deterministic when quarantine triggers mid-session.
Risk: Immediate customer-facing impact (model quality mismatch) and potential compliance concerns for Private/VPC tenants expecting strict pinning.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation (applied 2026-03-12 13:10 UTC): Disabled traffic-quarantine for NimbleDocs' edge cohort and rolled back canary weight to previous known-good to avoid further quarantines. Customer confirmed error incidence decreased.
Workaround guidance provided to customer: pin at proxy-level header + enable strict_route flag on tenant config to force edge to honor pin during fallback. Documented steps shared in support thread.

Planned fix: Patch edge quarantine code to preserve tenant_pin during fallback resolution (add PinReconciler call inside quarantine short-circuit). Patch PR prepared: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1024.

Deployment plan: staged rollout of patch to edge canaries with observability flags enabled. Monitor routing-audit and model-selection histograms for pinned tenants. Target deploy: 2026-03-16 (pending review).

Follow-ups: Add unit/integration tests for quarantine + pin interactions, update runbook to include pin preservation check, and add alert on discrepancy between tenant_pin and resolved_model in routing-audit.
